title: Surface Processes
short_title: weathering, mass wasting, streams, groundwater and glaciers
standard_text: Earth's surface is shaped by weathering, erosion and deposition: mechanical and chemical weathering, mass wasting, streams, groundwater, glaciation, and the landforms they produce in BC. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Geology 12)
meta_desc: Free Geology 12 worksheets (BC Curriculum): weathering, mass wasting, streams, groundwater and glaciers. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Weathering breaks rock; erosion moves it.
key_sub: Glaciers carved BC's U-shaped valleys and fjords.
body_html:
How to think about it

Mechanical weathering (frost wedging, abrasion) breaks rock into pieces; chemical weathering (oxidation, dissolution by acidic water) changes its minerals. Mass wasting is the downhill movement of rock and soil under gravity: landslides, slumps, rockfalls and debris flows.

Streams erode V-shaped valleys and deposit sediment in floodplains and deltas, like the Fraser River delta. Groundwater fills porous, permeable rock (aquifers). Glaciers erode U-shaped valleys, cirques and fjords and leave moraines and erratics.

Example

What shape of valley does a glacier carve?

Wide and flat-bottomed

Answer: U-shaped

Example

Water freezes in a crack and splits a rock. What process is this?

Ice expands.

Answer: frost wedging (mechanical weathering)

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up weathering and erosion.
  • Thinking only water causes erosion.
  • Thinking porosity and permeability are the same.

items.q: How does pumped hydro storage, such as Snowy 2.0, work?

the maximum amount that can be taken at once

items.q: What is a disadvantage of solar and wind power?

items.q: Water molecules stick to each other and to surfaces (cohesion and adhesion). Which effect on Earth's surface does this cause?
c: Ice in cracks pries rocks apart (frost wedging).
Rivers carry dissolved salts to the sea, making it salty.
It slowly dissolves limestone, forming caves and sinkholes.
Water rises through tiny spaces in soil by capillary action.
items.e: Water's unusual properties shape Earth's surface.

items.q: Which property of water explains this: It slowly dissolves limestone, forming caves and sinkholes.

Water molecules stick to each other and to surfaces (cohesion and adhesion).
Water has a very high heat capacity.
Ice is less dense than liquid water.
items.e: Match the effect to the property.

Ice is less dense than liquid water.

items.q: What is geothermal energy?

heat from inside Earth used for heating or to generate electricity
items.e: Iceland and New Zealand use a lot of it.

items.q: What is the Murray–Darling Basin Plan?
c: a plan to build a new river
a plan to share water between farms, towns and the environment so the river system stays healthy
a plan for mining in the basin
a plan to drain the rivers
items.e: It sets sustainable diversion limits.

items.q: What is groundwater?
c: water stored in pores and fractures of rock and sediment below the water table
items.e: Aquifers store groundwater.
